info.title: Economic Policy & System Information
info.description: Set the economic system spectrum, choose sector policies, and adjust ownership or nationalization levels for production sectors. These choices shape the economy and the state's share of profits.

command.title: Command Economy
command.description: The government has full control over prices, production quotas, and resource allocation. State-owned enterprises dominate every economic sector.

marketSocialism.title: Market Socialism
marketSocialism.description: The state controls vital sectors through strict regulation, while small and medium businesses may operate under capped returns.

mixed.title: Mixed Economy
mixed.description: A balance between government regulation and private-market freedom. The state manages essential public services.

regulatedMarket.title: Regulated Market
regulatedMarket.description: Private markets drive economic growth. The government focuses on competition oversight and macroeconomic stability.

laissezFaire.title: Laissez-Faire / Free Capitalism
laissezFaire.description: Full deregulation and unrestricted markets. Business competition follows the laws of supply and demand.

optionA.label: State Price Ceiling
optionA.effect: Prices remain stable, but the risk of shortages increases.

optionB.label: Free Market Pricing
optionB.effect: Goods remain plentiful, but sudden inflation spikes are more likely.

optionA.label: State Monopoly / Nationalization
optionA.effect: National treasury revenue rises, but operational efficiency falls.

optionB.label: Privatization & Private Investors
optionB.effect: Innovation and efficiency improve rapidly, but state royalties shrink.

optionA.label: Strict Protectionism
optionA.effect: Domestic industries are protected, but consumer choice is limited.

optionB.label: Free Trade
optionB.effect: Imports and exports grow quickly, but local industries face tougher competition.

optionA.label: High Minimum Wage & Strict Protections
optionA.effect: Workers' welfare improves, but foreign investment becomes less attractive.

optionB.label: Flexible Work & Open Contracts
optionB.effect: Employment rises, but social inequality may increase.

optionA.label: State Ownership & Communal Use
optionA.effect: The state owns land and housing; people receive communal usage rights.

optionB.label: Absolute Private Property Rights
optionB.effect: Land and property can be freely bought and sold.

optionA.label: State Unions & Workers' Councils
optionA.effect: Unions become state bodies, and collective worker councils participate in factory management.

optionB.label: Free Labor Market
optionB.effect: Private management leads; strikes may be restricted to keep supply chains running.

optionA.label: Single Central Bank & Currency Controls
optionA.effect: Banks are state-owned; currency is controlled and capital flight is restricted.

optionB.label: Private Banking & Free Capital Flows
optionB.effect: Competitive banking and unrestricted capital flows in and out.

marketFree.name: Free Market
marketFree.description: The private sector manages this sector; the state receives basic taxes and royalties.

strictRegulation.name: Strict Regulation
strictRegulation.description: The state regulates prices and quotas while private operators remain dominant.

mixed.name: Mixed Economy
mixed.description: The state holds a majority stake and oversees private operators.

stateDominance.name: State Dominance
stateDominance.description: The state controls nearly all productive assets.

fullNationalization.name: Full Nationalization
fullNationalization.description: All productive assets are managed by the state.
